ARCHITECTURAL KNOWLEDGE — RAG Pipeline Specification (MEOK.AI Blueprint 2026-03-19):

MEOK's current enhanced_memory.py uses numpy cosine similarity in-memory. The blueprint specifies production-grade RAG that MEOK should adopt incrementally.

PROPER RAG PIPELINE COMPONENTS:
1. Document ingestion: Unstructured parsers (PDF, HTML, Markdown) → chunk with 20% overlap
2. Embedding generation: Sentence Transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 or nomic-embed-text via Ollama)
3. Vector storage options (ranked by MEOK fit):
   a. pgvector (PostgreSQL extension) — BEST FIT: MEOK already uses Postgres, zero extra infra
   b. Redis for low-latency in-memory retrieval (MEOK has in-memory fallback already)
   c. Milvus with GPU acceleration — for post-launch scale (>1M episodes)
   d. Elasticsearch for hybrid BM25+dense search — enterprise tier
4. Retrieval: Hybrid BM25 + dense vector search → reranking with cross-encoder
5. Context injection: Top-K retrieved chunks prepended to LLM prompt

IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY FOR MEOK:
- Phase 1 (now): Enable pgvector extension in Postgres, add embedding column to memory_episodes
  SQL: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
  SQL: ALTER TABLE memory_episodes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS embedding vector(384);
  SQL: CREATE INDEX hnsw_idx ON memory_episodes USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
- Phase 2 (post-launch): Sentence Transformers embedding on record, HNSW index for recall
- Phase 3 (Q2): Hybrid BM25+dense, cross-encoder reranker, multi-index routing

KEY INSIGHT: The difference between in-memory cosine and pgvector HNSW:
- In-memory: O(n) linear scan, breaks at >10K episodes
- pgvector HNSW: O(log n) approximate, handles millions of episodes
- This is the single most impactful upgrade for MEOK memory quality at scale.

ARCHITECTURAL KNOWLEDGE — Prompt Engineering & LLM Security (MEOK.AI Blueprint 2026-03-19):

Blueprint Section 3.3 + 4.3: Prompt management and LLM-specific security.

PROMPT ENGINEERING SYSTEMS:
1. Prompt versioning: Store prompts with semantic version tags in DB
   - Each dream/briefing/care prompt has a version
   - A/B testing: split traffic between prompt versions, measure care_alignment delta
2. Dynamic templates: Jinja2 with entity context injection
   - Template: '{{ entity.name }} ({{ entity.hatch_name }}) needs: {{ care_context }}'
3. Few-shot example management: Pre-curated examples per task_type stored in memory
   - Code tasks → code examples; care tasks → care examples
   - Weighted by care_weight + recency

LLM SECURITY LAYERS (extending existing CodeInterpreter):
1. Prompt injection detection (add to CodeInterpreter Level 1):
   - Pattern match: 'ignore previous instructions', 'pretend you are', 'system prompt'
   - Detect in both code AND code comment strings
2. PII redaction before memory storage:
   - Regex patterns: email ([a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,})
   - Phone: (\+?[1-9]\d{1,14})
   - NHS number: (\d{3}[-\s]\d{3}[-\s]\d{4})
   - Replace with [PII_REDACTED] before record_episode()
3. Content safety classification:
   - Llama Guard (via Ollama) for content safety scoring on user inputs
   - NeMo Guardrails for topic control (stay in MEOK domain)
4. Model supply chain:
   - Verify Ollama model hashes before dream synthesis
   - SBOM tracking for LLM Router provider versions

WHAT TO BUILD NOW vs DEFER:
- NOW: Prompt injection detection in CodeInterpreter (extend existing _check_dangerous())
- NOW: PII redaction wrapper in enhanced_memory.record_episode()
- DEFER (Q2): Llama Guard integration, NeMo Guardrails, model signing

ARCHITECTURAL KNOWLEDGE — LLM-Specific Observability (MEOK.AI Blueprint 2026-03-19):

Blueprint Section 5: Monitoring, Logging, Observability for LLM systems.

LLM-SPECIFIC METRICS (beyond generic HTTP metrics):
1. TTFT (Time to First Token): ms from request to first token streamed
   - P50/P95/P99 per provider
   - Claude target: <500ms P95
   - Ollama target: <2000ms P95 (local model cold start)
2. TPOT (Time Per Output Token): ms per token in generation
   - Reveals model saturation under load
3. Token throughput: tokens/second per provider
4. Cache hit rate: % of requests served from KV cache
5. Model load time: cold start penalty
6. Context window utilization: avg tokens used / max context

IMPLEMENTATION FOR MEOK LLM ROUTER:
- Add to each completion call: record start_time, first_token_time (streaming), end_time
- Store in _usage_stats per provider: { ttft_ms, total_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd }
- Expose via get_llm_router_status tool (already exists, just extend the response)
- Surface in dashboard: provider comparison widget showing avg TTFT

STRUCTURED LOGGING:
- PII-masked prompt/response logging (truncate to 200 chars, redact emails)
- Correlation IDs: each LLM request gets UUID, links to task_id and memory_episode_id
- OpenTelemetry spans: instrument _call_claude(), _call_openai_compat(), _call_ollama()

SLO TARGETS FOR MEOK:
- Morning briefing generation: < 5 seconds total
- Care response: < 2 seconds (Claude primary)
- Dream synthesis: < 30 seconds (Ollama acceptable)
- Code interpreter: < 10 seconds per execution

ALERTING: If provider P95 TTFT exceeds 2x baseline → circuit breaker pre-trip warning

ARCHITECTURAL KNOWLEDGE — Enterprise Security Architecture Q2 Roadmap (MEOK.AI Blueprint 2026-03-19):

Blueprint Section 4: Defense-in-depth security. NOT for March 31 launch — Q2 2026 roadmap.

API GATEWAY LAYER (Q2):
- Kong API Gateway with LLM plugins: rate limiting per user, token quota enforcement
- NGINX Ingress with ModSecurity WAF: blocks SQL injection, XSS at perimeter
- Replace current JWT validation with OIDC/OAuth 2.0 (Keycloak or Auth0)
- Short-lived access tokens (15 min TTL), refresh token rotation

RUNTIME ISOLATION (Q2 — extends CodeInterpreter):
- CodeInterpreter Level 3 (when implemented): gVisor or Kata Containers
- Network namespace isolation: code execution cannot reach internet
- Seccomp profiles: block dangerous syscalls (mount, ptrace, fork bombs)
- Resource quotas: CPU/RAM limits per execution pod

SECRETS MANAGEMENT (Q2):
- HashiCorp Vault: replace env var API keys with Vault dynamic secrets
- External Secrets Operator: sync Vault secrets to Kubernetes Secrets
- Cloud KMS: encrypt database columns (memory_episodes.content) at rest
- Audit log every secret access

CONTENT SAFETY (Q2):
- Llama Guard 2 (via Ollama): classify inputs/outputs for safety categories
  - Supports: violence, hate speech, self-harm, illegal activity
  - Run async post-generation, flag but don't block by default
- NeMo Guardrails: topic rails to keep MEOK conversations on-domain
- PII detection: Microsoft Presidio for structured PII entity recognition

SERVICE MESH (Q3):
- Istio or Linkerd: mTLS between all MEOK microservices
- Traffic policies: circuit breakers at mesh level
- Distributed tracing: Jaeger/Tempo for request flows

CRITICAL NOTE: None of this blocks March 31 launch. Current JWT + subprocess sandboxing is sufficient for MVP. Enterprise security is a prerequisite for multi-tenant pro tier at scale.

ARCHITECTURAL KNOWLEDGE — Enterprise Infrastructure Q2-Q3 2026 Roadmap (MEOK.AI Blueprint 2026-03-19):

Blueprint Sections 2, 6-10: Kubernetes, model serving, fine-tuning, IaC. Full enterprise roadmap.

KUBERNETES FOUNDATION (Q2):
- Upgrade from Docker Compose to Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/AKS or on-prem k3s)
- Node pools: CPU nodes (API servers), GPU nodes (model serving), spot nodes (batch)
- KEDA: event-driven autoscaling on queue depth (TaskExecutor queue → scale workers)
- Storage: PVC for model artifacts, S3/MinIO for ephemeral code execution outputs

MODEL SERVING (Q2):
- vLLM: replace Ollama for production model serving
  - PagedAttention for efficient GPU memory
  - Continuous batching: 5-10x throughput vs naive serving
  - OpenAI-compatible API: drop-in for LLM Router _call_ollama()
- TensorRT-LLM: for NVIDIA GPU optimization (if GPU nodes available)
- KServe: Kubernetes-native model serving CRD
  - BaseModel CRD: { name, source, version, framework }
  - InferenceService CRD: { model_ref, runtime, scaling_config }

FINE-TUNING INFRASTRUCTURE (Q3):
- LoRA/QLoRA: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for MEOK-specific models
  - Use case: fine-tune a small model on MEOK entity conversations
  - Trains in hours on single GPU, 4-bit quantization via QLoRA
- Distributed training: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for larger models
- Kubeflow Pipelines: orchestrate train → evaluate → deploy workflows

INFRASTRUCTURE AS CODE:
- Terraform modules: EKS cluster, RDS Postgres, ElastiCache Redis, S3 buckets
- Helm charts: meok-server, meok-ui, meok-desktop-update-server
- GitOps: ArgoCD watches `meok-infra` repo → auto-deploys on merge to main
- Flux: multi-cluster sync for edge deployments (user self-hosted MEOK)

CI/CD:
- GitHub Actions: test → build Docker → push to ECR → ArgoCD sync
- Model testing: Garak for LLM vulnerability scanning before prod deployment
- Blue-green deployments: zero-downtime model updates

COST TARGETS:
- MVP (March 31): £50/mo (current VPS + Vercel)
- Pro tier 100 users: £200/mo (Postgres + Redis + GPU spot)
- Pro tier 1000 users: £1500/mo (EKS + multi-zone + reserved instances)

SELF-HOSTED MEOK (open source user path):
- Docker Compose (already done) → k3s single-node → full K8s cluster
- Users can run their own sovereign instance — this is the sovereignty promise
